-75.38450,40.66720.name: Family Fertility Center
-75.38450,40.66720.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: H. Christina Lee, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-78.48199,-0.16371.name: FertyINFES
-78.48199,-0.16371.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

54.37730,24.45390.name: Sovereign wealth investment in agrifood technology
54.37730,24.45390.desc: Gulf state funds have taken large positions in agricultural and food technology, including engineered crops and cultivated protein, driven by import dependence rather than by returns alone. State capital with a food-security motive behaves differently from venture capital with a fund clock, and it is becoming a significant share of the money in this field.

116.29000,40.07000.name: Pharmaron
116.29000,40.07000.desc: A Chinese contract research organisation running preclinical and clinical work for international pharmaceutical clients. A large share of the data Western regulators assess is generated in a country whose own oversight system those regulators do not administer.

-76.85000,39.10000.name: Advarra
-76.85000,39.10000.desc: A commercial institutional review board reviewing clinical trial ethics for sponsors who pay it, and one of two firms that between them review a very large share of US industry trials. Ethics review was designed to be done by a committee at the institution running the study; contracting it to a company chosen and paid by the sponsor is now the norm, and nothing about that arrangement is disclosed on the resulting publication.

-47.89190,-15.79750.name: CTNBio — Comissão Técnica Nacional de Biossegurança
-47.89190,-15.79750.state: Brasília — Esplanada dos Ministérios, Bloco E
-47.89190,-15.79750.desc: Brazil’s biosafety commission, which decides what may be released. It has approved more engineered events than any regulator outside the United States, and its 2018 resolution putting most gene-edited organisms outside the registration system is the carve-out this map records for Brazil.

-47.89190,-15.79750.name: Ministério Público Federal — Brasília
-47.89190,-15.79750.desc: In 2013 Brazil's federal public prosecutor opened a civil inquiry into possible illegalities in the biosafety commission's commercial release of soy and maize engineered to tolerate 2,4-D, glyphosate and glufosinate, naming the files then on the commission's agenda and the companies that would benefit from them. The prosecutor also asked the commission to approve no new engineered organisms until in-depth environmental and health studies had been done and a broad public discussion held. The mechanism is what makes it worth carrying: a civil inquiry is opened by a prosecutor on the prosecutor's own initiative, without a claimant, a plaintiff class or anyone who has yet been harmed. Where a country has an office like this, a regulator's decision can be examined by someone who did not have to be injured first to ask.

-47.89190,-15.79750.name: Conselho Nacional de Biosegurança (CNBS)
-47.89190,-15.79750.desc: Brazil's 2005 biosafety law restructured the technical commission and created a national biosafety council above it, along with a national biosafety policy. The commission decides on the science; the council sits over it and the commission reports to it. That two-tier design is unusual and worth knowing about wherever an approval is being contested, because it means a technical decision has a political body with authority over it, and civil society objections to the engineered wheat approval have been directed there as well as at the commission. A reader looking for where to object in Brazil needs both addresses, not one.

-47.89190,-15.79750.name: CTNBio — engineered eucalyptus approvals
-47.89190,-15.79750.state: Brasília — Comissão Técnica Nacional de Biossegurança
-47.89190,-15.79750.desc: Brazil is the only country to have released engineered trees for commercial-scale cultivation, and this commission is where every one of those decisions was taken. Event H421, which overexpresses an Arabidopsis gene to increase wood volume, was developed in 2000, field-tested under regulation from 2006 to 2015 across three states, and approved in 2015 as the first genetically modified eucalyptus approved anywhere. Nine approvals have followed: five herbicide-tolerant events since 2021, an insect-resistant Bt event in 2023, a double stack later that year and a triple stack in March 2024, the first anywhere. Post-release monitoring ran five consecutive years with annual reports. Eucalyptus covers roughly 7.5 million hectares in Brazil. Set this against New Zealand felling its trial trees at eight years and China unable to say how much poplar was planted: three regulators, three entirely different answers to the same organism.

-79.38300,43.65300.name: ETC Group
-79.38300,43.65300.desc: Produces the concentration figures on seed, pesticide and livestock genetics that almost every account of this industry uses, including this map's. A small organisation supplying the numbers both sides argue with is worth naming rather than citing invisibly.

-97.14700,49.90300.name: BSL4ZNET — Biosafety Level 4 Zoonotic Laboratory Network
-97.14700,49.90300.state: Winnipeg — National Microbiology Laboratory, 1015 Arlington Street
-97.14700,49.90300.desc: A dozen BSL4 laboratories in five countries sharing knowledge and training on zoonotic disease. Networks of this kind are the only routine contact between maximum containment facilities in different states: there is no inspectorate and no obligation to declare what is held, so a voluntary network is the nearest thing to mutual oversight that exists.
